## Purpose

This SOP describes the calibration, operation, and maintenance of
handheld nephelometric turbidity meters for field measurement of water
clarity. Turbidity is a standard water quality parameter required by
the Surface Water Ambient Monitoring Program (SWAMP), NPDES permits,
and many ecological studies [@apha2012]. Field measurements complement
laboratory analysis by providing an immediate on-site result.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Handheld nephelometric turbidity meters (e.g., Hach
  2100Q, LaMotte 2020we, Oakton T-100) used for in situ and
  grab-sample turbidity measurements at EA Program field sites
- **Does not apply to:** Laboratory bench-top turbidimeters; Secchi
  disk transparency measurements (see
  [SOP-F207](SOP-F207-secchi-disk.qmd)); continuous turbidity sensors
  on multiparameter sondes (see [SOP-F200](SOP-F200-eureka-manta2.qmd))
- **Location:** All EA Program surface water field sites


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| PI / Field Lead   | Approve instrument selection; review QC data            |
| Trained Personnel | Calibrate and operate the meter per this SOP            |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use                |


## Definitions

- **Formazin:** A synthetic polymer suspension used as the primary
  turbidity calibration standard; traceable to NIST; typically supplied
  as a 4000 NTU stock that is diluted to working standards; contains
  hydrazine and must be handled as hazardous waste [@apha2012].
- **Nephelometric turbidity:** Turbidity measured by the intensity of
  light scattered at 90° to an incident beam; the standard method per
  APHA Method 2130B; appropriate for samples with NTU < 40; for higher
  values a ratio or attenuation mode may be used [@apha2012].
- **NTU (Nephelometric Turbidity Units):** The unit of turbidity
  measured by a 90° nephelometer; numerically equivalent to FNU
  (Formazin Nephelometric Units) and approximately equivalent to FAU
  (Formazin Attenuation Units) at low concentrations [@apha2012].
- **RPD (relative percent difference):** |A - B| / ((A + B) / 2) × 100;
  used to assess duplicate precision; acceptance criterion for field
  turbidity duplicates is RPD < 20% for readings above 10 NTU.
- **Silicone oil treatment:** Application of a thin film of silicone
  oil to the outside of a glass sample vial before measurement to fill
  surface scratches and reduce spurious light scattering; standard
  practice for glass vial meters [@hach_2100q].
- **StablCal:** A sealed formazin-based calibration standard supplied
  by Hach; stable and ready to use without dilution; available in
  < 0.1, 20, 100, and 800 NTU vials.


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Sampling near water involves slip and fall hazards.
- **Biological:** Water samples may contain pathogens. Wear gloves.
- **Chemical:** Formazin calibration standards contain hydrazine, a
  suspected carcinogen. Handle with gloves; dispose of as hazardous
  waste. StablCal sealed standards eliminate direct hydrazine exposure.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves
- [ ] Safety glasses (during calibration with bulk formazin)
- [ ] Closed-toed shoes or wading boots

### Emergency Procedures

Refer to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd). For
formazin contact with skin or eyes, flush with water for at least
15 minutes and consult the SDS.


## Equipment and Materials

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Handheld turbidity meter              | Confirm model and battery level          |
| Calibration standards                 | Hach StablCal sealed vials: < 0.1, 20, 100, 800 NTU; or prepared formazin dilution series |
| Sample vials (matched to instrument)  | Glass or optical-grade; use only with the meter they were supplied with |
| Silicone oil and applicator cloth     | For glass vials [@hach_2100q]            |
| Lint-free wipes (Kimwipes)            | For cleaning vials                       |
| DI water (squeeze bottle)             | For rinsing vials and blanks             |
| Waste container (labeled hazardous)   | For used formazin waste                  |
| Field notebook                        | Per [SOP-F003](SOP-F003-field-notebook-protocols.qmd) |
| Spare batteries                       | Matched to meter model                   |


## Procedure

### Calibration

Calibrate at the start of each field day or after storage of more than
one week [@apha2012].

1. Turn on the meter and allow it to warm up (approximately 1 minute).
2. Clean calibration vial exteriors with a lint-free wipe. Apply a
   thin, even film of silicone oil for glass vials.
3. Insert the lowest standard (< 0.1 NTU) into the sample chamber
   with the orientation mark aligned. Close the lid.
4. Press **Cal** and follow the on-screen prompts to read the standard.
5. Repeat with each subsequent standard in ascending order
   (e.g., 20, 100, 800 NTU).
6. When all standards have been read, the meter confirms a successful
   calibration. Record the date, standard lot number, and any
   correction factors in the field notebook.
7. Verify calibration by re-reading the 20 NTU standard; the reading
   must be within ±10% of 20 NTU. If not, repeat the full calibration.

### Sample Collection

1. Collect a grab sample per
   [SOP-F300 Surface Water Sampling](SOP-F300-surface-water-sampling.qmd).
2. Avoid disturbing bottom sediments during collection.
3. Analyze as soon as possible; if delayed, keep the sample in the
   dark and analyze within 24 hours.

### Measurement

1. Gently invert the sample container 3--4 times to resuspend
   particles uniformly. Do not shake vigorously (creates air bubbles).
2. Pour the sample into a clean sample vial to the fill line.
3. Cap and let sit for 1 minute to allow large air bubbles to rise.
4. Wipe the outside of the vial with a lint-free cloth. Apply
   silicone oil for glass vials.
5. Insert the vial with the orientation mark aligned. Close the lid.
6. Press **Read** and wait for the display to stabilize.
7. Record the result (NTU), sample ID, time, and site in the field
   notebook.
8. For samples above the meter range (typically > 1000 NTU), dilute
   with DI water, measure, and multiply by the dilution factor.
   Record both the diluted reading and the corrected result.
9. Rinse the vial three times with DI water between samples.

### Post-Field Care

1. Rinse all sample vials with DI water; air-dry inverted.
2. Wipe silicone oil residue from vials before storage.
3. Store calibration standards in their original case, away from
   direct sunlight, at room temperature.
4. Turn off the meter; remove batteries if storing for more than one
   month.


## Quality Control

- Calibrate at the start of each field day (§6.1) [@apha2012].
- Measure a DI water blank at the start and end of each sampling
  event; the blank must read < 1 NTU.
- Measure one field duplicate per 10 samples (minimum one per event);
  duplicate RPD must be < 20% for readings above 10 NTU.
- If the DI blank drifts above 1 NTU during the day, recalibrate and
  re-measure the most recent samples.
- Inspect sample vials for scratches before each use; scratches
  scatter light and produce false-high readings.

## Training Record

Before using turbidity meters independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Demonstrate a complete calibration using StablCal or formazin
   standards
3. Perform supervised field measurements at one site
4. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
